blocks.text: An accurate description of this tree was given by Forsskål in the Flora Aegyptiaco-Arabica p. 37, under this name: "Sceura marina, with lanceolate, entire leaves and tawny flowers. Arab. Schura, شورة [shūra], among the people of Muscat Germ, قرم [qurm]. Frequent on the islands and shores of the Red Sea; it grows in dense woods, like the alder groves of the northern world." And Forsskål's description confirms that Bochart rightly takes this tree to be the same one of which Theophrastus, Pliny and Plutarch speak in the passages adduced above; the plan of our work, however, does not permit us to add it here.
Matth. III, 16. Marc. I, 10. Luc. III, 22. Ioh. I, 32.
What follows from here on, on the typological significance of Noah's dove, we have thought best to omit.
